stem: Which of the cyclic species labelled I–IV in the figure are aromatic according to Hückel’s rule?

verdicts.working: Top to bottom, then left to right: I has 8 π electrons and II has 4, so neither is aromatic. III (cyclopentadienyl anion) and IV (tropylium cation) each have 6 π electrons and satisfy Hückel’s rule.
issues: The figure does not visibly label the structures I–IV; this assumes they are ordered top-to-bottom, then left-to-right.

verdicts.working: I = cyclooctatetraene: 8 π e⁻ (4n), tub-shaped, non-aromatic. II = cyclobutadiene: 4 π e⁻, antiaromatic. III = cyclopentadienyl anion: 4 π e⁻ from two C=C + 2 from carbanion lone pair = 6 π e⁻ (4n+2, n=1), aromatic. IV = tropylium cation: 6 π e⁻ from three C=C, empty p on C⁺ keeps conjugation, aromatic. Hence III and IV only.

working:
I: $6\pi$ electrons; $4n+2$ for $n=1$ → aromatic.
II: $6\pi$ electrons; $4n+2$ for $n=1$ → aromatic.
III: $4\pi$ electrons; antiaromatic.
IV: $8\pi$ electrons; non-planar, non-aromatic.
solution:
A planar cyclic conjugated species is aromatic if it has $4n+2$ π electrons. I and II each have $6π$ electrons ($n=1$), so both are aromatic; III has $4π$ electrons and IV is non-planar.
Thus, I and II only.
